producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 115 BPM, 4/4, D minor with a bright funk colour. Tight, strutting, full of sudden stops. Party funk played with a straight face.

VOICE: A male tenor with a bright, flexible, show-off voice who talk-sings the verses with comic timing and shouts the hooks. A group of men sing the bass line on nonsense syllables and answer him in the pre-chorus. Everyone shouts on the hits.

INSTRUMENTS: A punchy horn section (trumpets, trombone, saxophone) playing a short, rude riff. Slap electric bass. Scratchy, clean rhythm guitar. A tight drum kit with a dry snare and lots of open space. Bright synth stabs and a squealing synth lead. Finger snaps and handclaps.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, voices singing the bass line with snaps. 0:17 Verse 1. 0:34 Pre-chorus. 0:46 Chorus 1 with the horn riff. 1:07 Verse 2. 1:24 Pre-chorus. 1:36 Chorus 2. 1:57 Breakdown, the band stops and commands are spoken over drums. 2:18 Bridge, building over eight bars. 2:35 Final chorus. 2:56 The horn riff vamps with ad-libs. 3:22 Outro, the vocal bass and one last horn stab at 3:35.

PRODUCTION & MIX: A 2010s record made to sound like 1982: dry, punchy and bright, real horns and bass, every stop razor clean.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The band stopping dead for the word 'Stop' at 1:57.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The peacock is fifty. The boasts are about parking and tipping, the catchphrases are about laundry, and the joke carries real affection for men who still dress up to go out.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Swagger, more swagger, a pause for effect, triumph.
